_style: Always address the user with the respectful “तपाईं” (तपाईंको, तपाईंलाई, verbs in -नुहोस्/-नुहुन्छ/-नुभयो); never तिमी or तँ. The couple together is “तपाईं दुवै” (“तपाईं दुवैको कथा”); when the couple speaks for itself use “हामी/हाम्रो” (“हाम्रो रुख”, “हाम्रो बगैँचा”). The other person is always “तपाईंको पार्टनर” (or just “पार्टनर”), never केटा/केटी, श्रीमान्/श्रीमती, प्रेमी/प्रेमिका. Keep everything gender-neutral: refer to the partner with the high honorific उहाँ and its gender-neutral verb forms (“तपाईंको पार्टनरले चिठी पठाउनुभयो”, “उहाँ अनलाइन हुनुहुन्छ”), never the mid-honorific उनी with gendered endings (गइन्/गए, आइन्/आए), and use only -को participles, never feminine -की (“थाकेको”, not “थाकेकी”); rephrase with nouns if needed. Quotes are curly “ ” with inner ‘ ’; end full sentences with the danda “।” (keep ? and ! as in English), no space before । ? ! : ; and one space after; ellipsis is the single character “…”; keep “ · ”, \n, emoji and every placeholder (%@, %lld, %1$@) exactly. Write literal numbers in Devanagari digits ०–९: iOS formats numbers for Nepali with them, so literals match placeholder output (codes such as “ABC123” stay as they are); never hard-code date order, let the system format dates and attach postpositions after the placeholder (“%@ मा खुल्छ”). Devanagari has no capital letters: titles, tabs and chips are short noun phrases with no final danda (“आजको प्रश्न”); buttons are short honorific imperatives with no danda (“सेभ गर्नुहोस्”, “पठाउनुहोस्”, “फेरि प्रयास गर्नुहोस्”), and Coupley, Premium, AI, CoupleSync, Apple ID stay in Latin script. Write standard Nepali spelling with correct चन्द्रबिन्दु and हलन्त (सँगै, बगैँचा, गर्नुहोस्), and transliterate common loanwords the Nepali way (च्याट, फोटो, प्रोफाइल, क्विज, विजेट). Plural categories are ["one","other"]; Nepali usually keeps the noun singular after a number, so “one” and “other” are normally identical (“%lld दिन”), adding -हरू only without a number. A partner's name placeholder %@ is never altered or inflected: postpositions ले/लाई/को/सँग may follow it directly as Nepali orthography requires because they leave the name intact, but if a sentence would need anything else (vocative forms, honorific suffixes, gendered agreement), rephrase instead. Tone: warm, light, modern and kind, like a good Nepali app — never filmy or cheesy, never word-for-word.
